blocks.html:
Module 3 of 5. Run a deep discovery conversation to find exactly what a client needs, then draw on the OneAccord community to serve it. You don't have to have every answer.

Here's how this module works: watch the video, work through a few short sections, answer a quick knowledge check, respond to a scenario (your coach grades it, and 3 of 4 points passes), then build one piece of your personal Sales Game Plan.

blocks.title: OneAccord Sales Video 3 - Qualifying Clients part 2 Leveraging Community

links.label: Video won't play? Open it in SharePoint

blocks.html:
1. Relationships transcend the transaction

  • Ask what else you can help with. Do they have the right banker, wealth advisor, accountant, attorney or insurance? Only ask if you mean it.
  • Use the community. When a snow-removal client couldn't get road salt, one note to the OneAccord community found a supplier. Needs and help flow both ways.
  • Don't fly solo. Working with others gives you objectivity, and it keeps you from being used by one owner against another.
  • Plenty mindset, not scarcity. If someone else is the best fit, refer them. More will come.

2. The discovery interview (30–60 minutes)

The prospect should do at least 70% of the talking. Cover the playbook's discovery areas: current objectives, challenges, what success looks like, decision drivers, timelines, and their strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, threats and dreams.

Then go deep on where the need actually sits:

AreaGo deeper: is it…Try asking
Revenue: salesSales development? A sales playbook? Building a sales org from scratch, including hiring?"Walk me through how a new customer finds you and buys today."
Revenue: marketingBranding? Messaging? Website? Content?"How would your best customer describe what makes you different?"
OperationsTechnology and systems? Physical operations or logistics?"Where do things get stuck or break as you grow?"
Leadership and teamA missing leader (fractional or interim)? Alignment among owners? Talent?"If you could add one leader tomorrow, what seat would it be?"
Finance and exitProfitability? Readiness for a sale? Succession?"If you sold in 3–5 years, what would need to be true?"

3. The OneAccord community

Twenty-five years have built a network of hundreds of professionals across disciplines. With the OneAccord brand behind you, you don't need every answer. We have a solution for almost any qualified client.

  • Bring 2–3 OneAccord teammates into early conversations when the need is outside your expertise.
  • Keeping opportunities outside your expertise to yourself is a trap. Connect the prospect to the right colleague or partner.
  • Where OneAccord doesn't serve a need directly (for example, full-time CFO or CHRO placement), we partner with firms that do.

OneAccord is the opposite of discord. Companies often underperform because owners or leaders aren't aligned. We bring alignment.

blocks.prompt: In a discovery interview, roughly how much should the prospect be talking?
blocks.feedbackCorrect: Right. Listen far more than you talk.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: Aim for the prospect talking at least 70% of the time.

blocks.prompt: An owner says, "Our sales are flat." What's the best next step?
options: Dig deeper: is it the sales process, marketing, operations or capacity?
blocks.feedbackCorrect: Exactly. Flat sales can come from sales, marketing or operations. Don't be a hammer looking for a nail.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: Dig deeper first. Flat sales might be an operations or marketing problem, not a sales one.

blocks.prompt: The need is mostly outside your expertise. What do you do?
options: Bring the right OneAccord teammate or partner into the conversation
blocks.feedbackCorrect: Correct. That's what the community is for.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: Bring in the right teammate or partner. You don't have to fly solo.

blocks.prompt: A co-owner asks you to back his side in a disagreement with his partner. What's the biggest risk?
options: Being used as one owner's advocate instead of serving the whole business
blocks.feedbackCorrect: Right. Stay objective. Bringing in a colleague helps.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: The risk is being used by one owner. Our value is alignment, not taking sides.

blocks.promptHtml:
In a first meeting, the owner of a $45M distributor says: "We're growing, but everything feels chaotic, and honestly I'm tired."

List the five discovery questions you'd ask next, and say who in the OneAccord community you might involve depending on the answers.
rubric: Questions probe at least two different areas (for example operations and leadership)
At least one question uncovers the owner's personal goals or 'dreams'
Names a sensible way to involve the OneAccord community rather than solving it alone
